skill.name: recoup-platform-build-os
skill.description: Scaffold and run a label's self-managing "music-company OS" inside its own git repo — the full label-intelligence workspace (folders, a self-managing CLAUDE.md mirrored to AGENTS.md, a read-only doctor + never-stale janitor, compound-learning and self-improvement loops, an in-place plugin) seeded with Recoup's conventions (top-level artists/{slug}/RECOUP.md identity files, releases/{slug}/RELEASE.md) and backed by the Recoup API as system of record. Use for "set up our label OS", "build the org workspace", "turn this repo into our label brain", or onboarding a new org/label repo. Pulls the real roster from the live account (auth via recoup-platform-connect-account), onboards artists API-first via recoup-roster-add-artist, and calls the other recoup-* skills (research/content/release/song/catalog) instead of reinventing them. The single workspace/OS builder — also covers the lightweight "just mirror my roster into folders" case.
skill.summary: Build a Recoup-backed operating workspace for an independent label, including roster folders, maintenance workflows, health checks, and agent plugin packaging.
skill.author: recoupable

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, documented project paths, and read-only workspace checks. Confirmed risks include persistent scheduled agent execution, predictable temporary archive paths, and access to a user-scoped credential file. The provided schedule can commit and push broad repository changes unattended.

remediation.issue: The scheduled workflow stages all changes and pushes directly after an autonomous agent run.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict staged paths, create a review branch, scan for secrets, and require approval before any remote push.

remediation.issue: Cron and LaunchAgent examples create persistent shell-based agent execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep scheduling opt-in, use fixed executable arguments, limit permissions, and document clear disable and rollback steps.

remediation.issue: Authentication may load credentials from a user-scoped hidden file.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit consent before credential access and limit reads to documented Recoup variables through the dedicated connection skill.

remediation.issue: Plugin archives use predictable filenames in the shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mktemp, reject links, and move the completed archive atomically.

content.user_title: Build a Recoup Label Workspace OS
content.value_statement: Label knowledge, roster data, and recurring work often become fragmented across tools. This skill builds a structured workspace connected to Recoup workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates a label workspace with artist, release, knowledge, work, artifact, plugin, and operations areas.
Uses companion Recoup skills to connect an account and mirror the live artist roster.
Generates customized CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md guidance for consistent agent behavior.
Creates doctor, janitor, learning, reflection, skill promotion, and intake workflows.
Builds Claude and Codex plugin manifests and prepares a distributable plugin archive.
Provides GitHub Actions, cron, LaunchAgent, and agent-runner scheduling examples for maintenance.
limitations: Live roster setup requires valid Recoup credentials and the referenced companion Recoup skills.
Scheduler examples require manual configuration and can run editing agents without supervision.
The workflow makes broad repository changes and should run only in a dedicated, reviewed workspace.
Health checks verify workspace structure but cannot guarantee business data accuracy.

use_cases.title: Launch a Label Workspace
use_cases.description: Create a structured operating repository from label notes, roster data, and existing project files.

use_cases.title: Mirror a Live Roster
use_cases.description: Connect Recoup and create consistent artist identity and release folders from the current account.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Operations
use_cases.description: Package label-specific maintenance and knowledge workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Build our label workspace in this repository using the available kickoff files. Show assumptions before connecting Recoup.

prompt_templates.title: Mirror the Roster
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect our Recoup account, inventory the roster, and create missing artist folders without overwriting existing material.

prompt_templates.title: Add Maintenance Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the doctor and janitor workflows, run the health check, and explain every proposed automatic repair.

prompt_templates.title: Package and Review Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate and package the label plugin. Review scheduler permissions, credential access, temporary files, and remote push behavior before enabling anything.

output_examples.input: Build a workspace from our roster export, release notes, and label operating documents.
output: Understanding brief covering the label, roster, release lifecycle, recurring work, and assumptions.
Structured artist, release, knowledge, work, artifact, plugin, and operations areas.
Health report listing completed checks, unresolved facts, and recommended next actions.

output_examples.input: Turn our repeated release review process into a reusable label skill.
output: A staged skill proposal with clear triggers, provenance, workflow steps, and verification evidence.
A review request before publication into the label plugin.
An updated package plan after approval.

output_examples.input: Check whether our label workspace is current and internally consistent.
output_examples.output: A scored health report covering roster folders, release state, manifests, skill reachability, package freshness, and maintenance scheduling.

best_practices: Review the understanding brief and inferred facts before allowing live Recoup changes.
Commit a clean baseline before scaffolding so every generated change is easy to inspect.
Keep scheduled automation disabled until permissions, staged paths, secret handling, and push behavior are reviewed.
anti_patterns: Do not place real credentials in the repository or generated example files.
Do not run the builder in a repository containing unrelated projects or unreviewed sensitive files.
Do not enable unattended commits, pushes, or external synchronization without narrow scope and approval controls.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Recoup account?
faq.answer: Yes for live roster synchronization. Structural workspace generation can use provided files, but Recoup-backed identity data requires valid account access.

faq.question: Which agent tools are supported?
faq.answer: The generated workspace includes conventions and plugin manifests for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and compatible project skill discovery.

faq.question: Will it overwrite existing artist files?
faq.answer: The workflow instructs agents to skip existing roster folders and reconcile material. Review changes because broad workspace edits remain possible.

faq.question: Does it enable scheduled maintenance automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides scheduler templates and requests a recorded cadence. Users must explicitly configure and enable a scheduler.

faq.question: Where should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Use approved environment storage outside the shared repository. Keep only variable names in .env.example and confirm access before loading credentials.

faq.question: How is the generated workspace verified?
faq.answer: A generated doctor checks structure, manifests, skill reachability, package freshness, dashboard presence, and selected consistency rules.
